focus_areas: Surface texture realism of the chocolate ice cream (plastic vs. creamy)
Physical interaction between melting ice cream and the wafer/hand (surface tension, dripping)
Boundary sharpness between the subject and the blurred background
Anatomical correctness of the hand holding the wafer
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'plastic' sheen on the chocolate scoop. Real ice cream usually has some micro-texture or frost, whereas this looks like smooth rendered plastic. Also, examine the contact points between the fingers and the wafer/ice cream for any fusion or unnatural smearing. The whipped cream on top also lacks detailed structure, looking like a single smooth blob.
image_description: A close-up shot of a chocolate ice cream scoop resting on a white wafer or cookie, held by a human hand. The ice cream is glossy, dark brown, and appears to be melting slightly, with some sauce or melted ice cream dripping onto the wafer and fingers. There is a dollop of white whipped cream on top of the chocolate scoop. The background is blurred, suggesting a shallow depth of field.

expert_testimonies.reason: To verify the spatial relationship between the hand, wafer, and scoop, ensuring the grip looks physically plausible and not fused.
To confirm the object is correctly classified as ice cream and not a similar-looking object like a chocolate truffle or clay model.
To check for boundary bleeding between the melting ice cream, the wafer, and the hand, ensuring distinct physical separation.
To assess the overall realism, focusing on the plastic-like texture of the ice cream and the naturalness of the lighting/reflections.
